description: Fig. 11 is a composite of eight bright-field TEM micrographs of the Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C (wt%) austenitic low-density steel after tension-tension fatigue, arranged as four rows (alloy/condition) by two columns (stress amplitude). The left column (a,c,e,g) is at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa and the right column (b,d,f,h) at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa. Rows give ST (a,b), 550-6 (c,d), 600-6 (e,f) and 650-6 (g,h). Panels (a) and (b) carry 1 µm scale bars and are labelled "PLBs" (persistent Lüder's bands) in red, with red arrows marking dense dark dislocation bands aligned along primary slip planes in a lighter matrix. Panels (c)-(h) carry 500 nm scale bars and are labelled "Planar slip bands" in blue, with blue dashed lines tracing the band traces across regions of comparatively uniform, finely structured planar arrays. Dislocation density and band contrast are visibly highest in the ST panels (a,b) and lowest and most uniformly distributed in the aged panels (c-h); band spacing appears narrower at the higher stress amplitude. No crystallographic indices, zone axes or diffraction patterns are labelled. The group argues that κ-carbide-containing aged alloys replace localized PLBs with a more uniform planar-slip network, consistent with their improved fatigue resistance.

observations.observation: The figure is a 4 x 2 composite of eight bright-field TEM micrographs; rows are the four conditions and columns are the two stress amplitudes.
Panels (a) and (b) carry 1 µm scale bars, while panels (c)-(h) carry 500 nm scale bars.
Panels (a) and (b) are annotated 'PLBs' in red with red arrows pointing to dense dark dislocation bands in a lighter matrix.
Panels (c) through (h) are annotated 'Planar slip bands' in blue, with blue dashed lines tracing the band orientations; no dashed lines appear in (a) or (b).
The caption states the panels are bright-field TEM micrographs of the ST (a,b), 550-6 (c,d), 600-6 (e,f) and 650-6 (g,h) samples fatigued at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa (a,c,e,g) and Δσ/2 = 315 MPa (b,d,f,h).
The citing text asserts that planar dislocation slip is the dominant deformation mechanism in all cases shown.

The citing text asserts that at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa the ST sample shows well developed persistent Lüder's bands (PLBs) made of dense dislocation arrays aligned along primary slip planes, indicating strain localization.

The citing text asserts that the aged samples show substantially lower overall dislocation density and more uniformly distributed planar slip bands than the ST sample because fine intragranular κ-carbides impede dislocation slip and accumulation.
The citing text asserts that at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa all samples show features similar to those at 180 MPa but with narrower slip band spacing and more extensive dislocation movement.
In the pixels, panels (a) and (b) show broader, higher-contrast dark bands than panels (c)-(h), whose contrast is finer and more evenly distributed.
Within each row, the 315 MPa panel shows a visibly finer, more closely spaced banded contrast than its 180 MPa counterpart, matching the caption's stress-amplitude pairing.
No crystallographic indices, zone axes, g-vectors, foil normals or diffraction patterns are labelled on any panel, so the specific slip systems cannot be read from the figure.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of the ST sample fatigued at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa; 1 µm scale bar. Dense dark dislocation bands labelled 'PLBs' with red arrows, aligned along primary slip planes within a lighter matrix; coarse, high-contrast banded structure.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the ST sample fatigued at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa; 1 µm scale bar. Same coarse dark PLB banding as (a) but with red arrows and 'PLBs' label marking narrower, more closely spaced bands.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 550-6 sample fatigued at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa; 500 nm scale bar. Blue dashed lines mark 'Planar slip bands'; fine, uniformly distributed planar slip traces with lower overall dislocation density than the ST sample.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 550-6 sample fatigued at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa; 500 nm scale bar. Three blue dashed lines label 'Planar slip bands' running roughly parallel across a finely structured region.
Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 600-6 sample fatigued at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa; 500 nm scale bar. Two blue dashed lines label 'Planar slip bands' in a region of uniform, wavy planar slip contrast.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 600-6 sample fatigued at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa; 500 nm scale bar. Blue dashed lines label 'Planar slip bands'; banded contrast is finer and more closely spaced than in the 180 MPa counterpart.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 650-6 sample fatigued at Δσ/2 = 180 MPa; 500 nm scale bar. Two blue dashed lines label 'Planar slip bands' drawn on a strongly striped, closely spaced planar-band texture.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the 650-6 sample fatigued at Δσ/2 = 315 MPa; 500 nm scale bar. Three-blue-dashed-line annotation 'Planar slip bands' over coarse striped contrast; band spacing appears narrower than at 180 MPa.

unreadable_items: No scale-bar-free quantitative measure is printed: dislocation density, band spacing and band width are not given numerically on any panel
Individual κ-carbide particles are not resolvable at the supplied resolution; their presence is only asserted by the caption/citing text
Slip-plane indices, zone axes and diffraction vectors for the blue dashed 'Planar slip bands' lines are not labelled
